articles.title: Reliance Industries to dissolve Hamleys Franchising subsidiary in UK
Reliance Industries seen posting double-digit Q2FY27 EBITDA growth on strong O2C, Jio performance
Reliance Industries Q2 Results: Profit shoots up 41% YoY to Rs 25,548 crore, revenue surges 29%
Reliance Industries Q2 net rises 34% to Rs 29,550 crore
Reliance Industries shares down 26% in 2026: Here’s how to trade RIL stocks on results day

article_briefs.brief: Reliance announced the voluntary strike‑off and dissolution of its step‑down subsidiary Hamleys (Franchising) Ltd in the UK, which had a turnover of Rs 56.08 crore in FY 2025 and zero net worth as of 31 Dec 2025. It will be struck off not less than two months from 27 Oct 2026.

Brokerage estimates project Reliance Industries to deliver double‑digit EBITDA growth in Q2 FY27, with O2C EBITDA expected to rise 12 % qoq and 38 % yoy, supported by strong Singapore gross refining margins, while retail is forecast to lag and Jio Platforms is slated for steady growth after its recent IPO.

In Q2 FY27 Reliance posted a 41 % YoY profit increase to Rs 25,548 crore, revenue up 29 % to Rs 3.32 lakh crore, O2C EBITDA surged 68 % YoY to Rs 25,203 crore, and the board authorised up to Rs 15,000 crore of non‑convertible debentures.

Reliance’s Q2 FY27 net profit rose 34 % to Rs 29,550 crore, revenue exceeded Rs 3.3 lakh crore, O2C EBITDA jumped 68 % YoY to Rs 25,203 crore, Jio Platforms EBITDA grew 18 % to Rs 22,223 crore, retail EBITDA fell 10 %, capex was Rs 38,153 crore, and the board approved a Rs 15,000 crore NCD issue.

The article provides technical analysis of Reliance’s share price ahead of the Q2 results, highlighting support and resistance levels and recent trading patterns, without reporting new corporate or sector developments.

key_points.text: Reliance is dissolving its step‑down subsidiary Hamleys (Franchising) Ltd in the UK following a voluntary strike‑off application; the entity reported a turnover of Rs 56.08 crore in FY 2025 and had nil net worth as of 31 Dec 2025.

Brokerages expect Reliance to post double‑digit Q2 FY27 EBITDA growth, with O2C EBITDA projected to rise 12 % quarter‑on‑quarter and 38 % year‑on‑year, driven by strong Singapore gross refining margins, while retail is forecast to be muted and Jio Platforms to deliver steady growth after its IPO.

Reliance reported Q2 FY27 profit up 41 % YoY to Rs 25,548 crore and revenue up 29 % to Rs 3.32 lakh crore; O2C EBITDA increased 68 % YoY to Rs 25,203 crore; the board authorized issuance of non‑convertible debentures up to Rs 15,000 crore.

Reliance reported Q2 FY27 net profit up 34 % to Rs 29,550 crore and revenue over Rs 3.3 lakh crore; O2C EBITDA rose 68 % YoY to Rs 25,203 crore; Jio Platforms EBITDA grew 18 % YoY to Rs 22,223 crore; retail EBITDA fell 10 %; capex totaled Rs 38,153 crore; board approved Rs 15,000 crore NCD raise.
The profit figures for Q2 FY27 differ between reports: one cites profit of Rs 25,548 crore, whereas another cites net profit of Rs 29,550 crore.

industry_context.text: Global refining margins have strengthened sharply amid supply disruptions in the Middle East and Russia, boosting O2C margins and contributing to higher earnings for integrated refiners.
